title: Sprint-slate entropy reduction and rollforward plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle sprint slates are suffering high entropy (scope churn, ad-hoc asks, and reprioritization) which reduces delivery predictability and increases blocker handoffs across product, eng, and design. This ticket defines a lightweight operational playbook to measure slate entropy, execute an evidence-driven rollforward or eviction of work, and create a small warm pool of prioritized quick-win items to absorb partial capacity.

Goals:
- Establish an entropy score (metric) for each sprint slate to guide decisions.
- Create a 3-tier decision tree (Protect, Defer, Evict) using quantitative thresholds and qualitative guardrails.
- Define staffing fallback roles (floaters/flex engineers + design partner) and a warm pool of tasks to soak residual capacity.
- Produce a one-page runbook for PMs and Eng leads to run during mid-cycle reviews.

Scope: Applies to product cycles with interleaved initiatives and teams with shared platform dependencies (runtime, console, infra). Not intended to be used for hotfix/incident work.

Why different: Rather than only trimming scope by priority, this playbook codifies an entropy signal (rate of scope changes + external interrupts + unknowns) and couples it to explicit rollforward actions (eviction list, deferred tranche) with staffing fallback commitments to reduce friction and preserve momentum.
acceptance_criteria: Entropy score defined and documented with calculation examples
Three-tier decision tree documented with example scenarios
Runbook one-pager created and reviewed by Eng and Design leads
Warm-pool backlog of at least 6 scoped quick-win tasks exists and owner-assigned
Pilot mid-cycle review executed in 2 product engineering pods and feedback collected
tasks: Define entropy metric: fields, weights, and sample calculation (owner: Marcus Chen)
Draft decision tree with thresholds and guardrails (owner: Aisha Patel)
Identify and triage warm-pool tasks (owner: Product ops)
Document runbook and PRD (Confluence) and link to dashboards (owner: PM)
Pilot with two pods, collect telemetry (SLO/throughput/blocked count) for 2 weeks

decisions: Use a composite entropy score = (scope_changes*0.4) + (external_interrupts*0.35) + (blocked_count*0.25) with 72h smoothing
Warm-pool size set to 6 items per pod, each scoped to <= 3 days of engineer effort
Floaters: 1 flex engineer and 1 design partner per two pods during mid-cycle windows
Eviction communication: PM sends eviction digest with rationale and alternative deferred tranche within 24h
